subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` calls fail closed on legacy ownerless rows without a migration, matching the existing exact-ownership rule used by `sessions.delete`?
rationale: Exact owner equality prevents an arbitrary plugin from adopting ambiguous persisted rows, but it intentionally makes a previously usable legacy row class inaccessible to plugin-runtime patch callers after upgrade.

options.title: Match delete and fail closed
options.body: Accept exact ownership for patch and require deployed proof that operator or non-plugin recovery remains available.

options.title: Migrate legacy ownership first
options.body: Add a narrow doctor or explicit operator path to assign ownership before rejecting plugin-runtime patch calls.

recommendation.title: Match delete and fail closed
recommendation.body: Accept exact ownership for patch and require deployed proof that operator or non-plugin recovery remains available.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently maintained the shared session store and accessor transaction boundary where the policy is now enforced.
